sanskrit: hanta vakṣyāmi te śreyaḥ śrutvā ca kuru tat tathā śaraṇāgatasaṃtrātā bhava kānta viśeṣataḥ
english: Listen, I will tell you what is best for you; hear it, and act accordingly. Above all, my beloved, be a protector of one who has come to you for refuge.

sanskrit: eṣa śākunikaḥ śete tava vāsaṃ samāśritaḥ śītārtaś ca kṣudhārtaś ca pūjām asmai prayojaya
english: This fowler lies here, having taken shelter in your dwelling, tormented by cold and afflicted by hunger; offer him due hospitality.

sanskrit: yo hi kaś cid dvijaṃ hanyād gāṃ vā lokasya mātaram śaraṇāgataṃ ca yo hanyāt tulyaṃ teṣāṃ ca pātakam
english: For whoever should slay a brāhmaṇa, or a cow—mother of the world—or one who has come for refuge: the sin of these is one and the same.

sanskrit: yāsmākaṃ vihitā vṛttiḥ kāpotī jātidharmataḥ sā nyāyyātmavatā nityaṃ tvadvidhenābhivartitum
english: That mode of life ordained for us pigeons by the law of our kind is one to be ever followed in righteousness by a self-possessed creature such as you.

sanskrit: yas tu dharmaṃ yathāśakti gṛhastho hy anuvartate sa pretya labhate lokān akṣayān iti śuśruma
english: A householder who follows dharma to the best of his power attains, after death, the imperishable worlds—so we have heard.

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ saṃtānavān adya putravān api ca dvija tat svadehe dayāṃ tyaktvā dharmārthau parigṛhya vai pūjām asmai prayuṅkṣva tvaṃ prīyetāsya mano yathā
english: You, O twice-born, are now blessed with offspring and have sons besides; therefore, casting off all tenderness for your own body and embracing dharma and its purpose, offer this man hospitality, so that his heart may be pleased.

sanskrit: iti sā śakunī vākyaṃ kṣārakasthā tapasvinī atiduḥkhānvitā procya bhartāraṃ samudaikṣata
english: Having spoken these words while caught in the snare-cage, the wretched hen-bird, overwhelmed with grief, gazed upon her husband.

sanskrit: sa patnyā vacanaṃ śrutvā dharmayuktisamanvitam harṣeṇa mahatā yukto bāṣpavyākulalocanaḥ
english: Hearing his wife's words, charged with the reasoning of dharma, he was filled with great joy, his eyes brimming with tears.

sanskrit: taṃ vai śākunikaṃ dṛṣṭvā vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā pūjayām āsa yatnena sa pakṣī pakṣijīvinam
english: Looking upon that fowler, the bird honored him diligently with the rites prescribed by ordinance—the bird honoring the one who lived by killing birds.

sanskrit: uvāca ca svāgataṃ te brūhi kiṃ karavāṇy aham saṃtāpaś ca na kartavyaḥ svagṛhe vartate bhavān
english: And he said: "Welcome to you. Tell me, what may I do for you? You must feel no distress; you are now within your own home."

sanskrit: tad bravītu bhavān kṣipraṃ kiṃ karomi kim icchasi praṇayena bravīmi tvāṃ tvaṃ hi naḥ śaraṇāgataḥ
english: "Speak quickly, sir—what shall I do, what do you desire? I say this to you out of affection, for you have come to us for refuge."

sanskrit: śaraṇāgatasya kartavyam ātithyam iha yatnataḥ pañcayajñapravṛttena gṛhasthena viśeṣataḥ
english: "Hospitality must be shown with care to one who has come for refuge, and most especially by a householder devoted to the five sacrifices."

sanskrit: pañcayajñāṃs tu yo mohān na karoti gṛhāśramī tasya nāyaṃ na ca paro loko bhavati dharmataḥ
english: "The householder who, through delusion, does not perform the five sacrifices wins, by the law, neither this world nor the next."

sanskrit: tad brūhi tvaṃ suvisrabdho yat tvaṃ vācā vadiṣyasi tat kariṣyāmy ahaṃ sarvaṃ mā tvaṃ śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: "So speak with full confidence; whatever you ask in words, all of it I shall do. Do not let your mind dwell in sorrow."

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā śakuner lubdhako 'bravīt bādhate khalu mā śītaṃ himatrāṇaṃ vidhīyatām
english: Hearing these words of the bird, the fowler replied: "The cold indeed torments me; let some protection against the frost be arranged."

sanskrit: evam uktas tataḥ pakṣī parṇāny āstīrya bhūtale yathāśuṣkāṇi yatnena jvalanārthaṃ drutaṃ yayau
english: Thus addressed, the bird, having carefully spread out such dry leaves as he could upon the ground for kindling a fire, swiftly went off.

sanskrit: sa gatvāṅgārakarmāntaṃ gṛhītvāgnim athāgamat tataḥ śuṣkeṣu parṇeṣu pāvakaṃ so 'bhyadīdipat
english: Going to a charcoal-burner's place, he fetched fire and returned; then upon the dry leaves he kindled the flame into a blaze.

sanskrit: susaṃdīptaṃ mahat kṛtvā tam āha śaraṇāgatam pratāpaya suvisrabdhaṃ svagātrāṇy akutobhayaḥ
english: Having made a great, well-blazing fire, he said to the refuge-seeker: "Warm your limbs in full confidence and without any fear."

sanskrit: sa tathoktas tathety uktvā lubdho gātrāṇy atāpayat agnipratyāgataprāṇas tataḥ prāha vihaṃgamam
english: So addressed, the fowler said "So be it" and warmed his limbs; his life-breath restored by the fire, he then said to the bird:

sanskrit: dattam āhāram icchāmi tvayā kṣud bādhate hi mām tad vacaḥ sa pratiśrutya vākyam āha vihaṃgamaḥ
english: "I wish for food to be given by you, for hunger torments me." Hearing his words, the bird answered:

sanskrit: na me 'sti vibhavo yena nāśayāmi tava kṣudhām utpannena hi jīvāmo vayaṃ nityaṃ vanaukasaḥ
english: "I have no store of wealth by which I might dispel your hunger, for we forest-dwellers live always upon whatever comes to hand."

sanskrit: saṃcayo nāsti cāsmākaṃ munīnām iva kānane ity uktvā sa tadā tatra vivarṇavadano 'bhavat
english: "We keep no hoard, like the sages in the wood." Having spoken thus, the bird's face turned pale.

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu khalu kartavyam iti cintāparaḥ sadā babhūva bharataśreṣṭha garhayan vṛttim ātmanaḥ
english: "How then is this to be done?"—sunk in this anxious thought, O best of the Bhāratas, he kept reproaching his own way of life.

sanskrit: muhūrtāl labdhasaṃjñas tu sa pakṣī pakṣighātakam uvāca tarpayiṣye tvāṃ muhūrtaṃ pratipālaya
english: But after a moment, regaining his composure, the bird said to the slayer of birds: "I shall satisfy you; wait but a moment."

sanskrit: ity uktvā śuṣkaparṇaiḥ sa saṃprajvālya hutāśanam harṣeṇa mahatā yuktaḥ kapotaḥ punar abravīt
english: Having said this, the pigeon, kindling the fire to a blaze with dry leaves, filled with great joy, spoke again:

sanskrit: devānāṃ ca munīnāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ ca mahātmanām śrutapūrvo mayā dharmo mahān atithipūjane
english: "From the gods, from the sages, and from the great-souled ancestors I have heard before of the supreme dharma that lies in honoring a guest."

sanskrit: kuruṣvānugrahaṃ me 'dya satyam etad bravīmi te niścitā khalu me buddhir atithipratipūjane
english: "Grant me this favor today—truly I tell you this: my resolve is fixed upon honoring my guest."

sanskrit: tataḥ satyapratijño vai sa pakṣī prahasann iva tam agniṃ triḥ parikramya praviveśa mahīpate
english: Then the bird, true to his vow, as if smiling, circumambulated that fire three times and entered into it, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: agnimadhyaṃ praviṣṭaṃ taṃ lubdho dṛṣṭvātha pakṣiṇam cintayām āsa manasā kim idaṃ nu kṛtaṃ mayā
english: Seeing the bird enter into the midst of the fire, the fowler reflected in his mind: "What is this I have brought about?"

sanskrit: aho mama nṛśaṃsasya garhitasya svakarmaṇā adharmaḥ sumahān ghoro bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Alas, for me, a cruel man, contemptible by reason of my own deeds, a most great and terrible sin will surely come—there is no doubt."

sanskrit: evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ bhūri vilalāpa sa lubdhakaḥ garhayan svāni karmāṇi dvijaṃ dṛṣṭvā tathāgatam
english: In many ways and at great length the fowler lamented thus, reproaching his own deeds, as he beheld the twice-born bird come to such an end.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tatas taṃ lubdhakaḥ paśyan kṛpayābhipariplutaḥ kapotam agnau patitaṃ vākyaṃ punar uvāca ha
english: Bhīṣma said: Then the fowler, watching the pigeon fallen into the fire and overwhelmed with pity, spoke again these words:

sanskrit: kim īdṛśaṃ nṛśaṃsena mayā kṛtam abuddhinā bhaviṣyati hi me nityaṃ pātakaṃ hṛdi jīvataḥ
english: "What a thing have I, a cruel and witless man, done! For as long as I live this sin will dwell forever in my heart."

sanskrit: sa vinindann athātmānaṃ punaḥ punar uvāca ha dhiṅ mām astu sudurbuddhiṃ sadā nikṛtiniścayam śubhaṃ karma parityajya yo 'haṃ śakunilubdhakaḥ
english: Reviling himself, he said again and again: "Shame upon me, the dull-witted, ever bent upon treachery, who, abandoning every good deed, became a hunter of birds!"

sanskrit: nṛśaṃsasya mamādyāyaṃ pratyādeśo na saṃśayaḥ dattaḥ svamāṃsaṃ dadatā kapotena mahātmanā
english: "This is, beyond doubt, a rebuke to me, a cruel man—delivered by the great-souled pigeon who gave his own flesh."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ tyakṣye priyān prāṇān putradāraṃ visṛjya ca upadiṣṭo hi me dharmaḥ kapotenātidharmiṇā
english: "I shall give up my own dear life and forsake my children and wife, for dharma has been taught to me by that supremely righteous pigeon."

sanskrit: adya prabhṛti dehaṃ svaṃ sarvabhogair vivarjitam yathā svalpaṃ jalaṃ grīṣme śoṣayiṣyāmy ahaṃ tathā
english: "From this day forth I shall dry up my own body, stripped of all enjoyments, as the scant water of summer is dried away."

sanskrit: kṣutpipāsātapasahaḥ kṛśo dhamanisaṃtataḥ upavāsair bahuvidhaiś cariṣye pāralaukikam
english: "Enduring hunger, thirst, and heat, grown gaunt with veins drawn taut, I shall pursue, through fasts of many kinds, the way to the world beyond."

sanskrit: aho dehapradānena darśitātithipūjanā tasmād dharmaṃ cariṣyāmi dharmo hi paramā gatiḥ dṛṣṭo hi dharmo dharmiṣṭhair yādṛśo vihagottame
english: "Lo, by the offering of his body, the honoring of a guest has been shown! Therefore I shall practice dharma, for dharma is the supreme goal—I have seen what dharma is, such as the righteous practice it, in that best of birds."

sanskrit: evam uktvā viniścitya raudrakarmā sa lubdhakaḥ mahāprasthānam āśritya prayayau saṃśitavrataḥ
english: Having spoken thus and made his resolve, the fowler of cruel deeds, taking up the Great Departure, set forth with a vow firmly fixed.

sanskrit: tato yaṣṭiṃ śalākāś ca kṣārakaṃ pañjaraṃ tathā tāṃś ca baddhā kapotān sa saṃpramucyotsasarja ha
english: Then his staff, his sticks, his snare, and his cage—and the pigeons he had bound—he loosed and set free.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato gate śākunike kapotī prāha duḥkhitā saṃsmṛtya bhartāram atho rudatī śokamūrchitā
english: Bhīṣma said: When the fowler had gone, the grieving hen-pigeon, remembering her husband and weeping, fainting with sorrow, spoke:

sanskrit: nāhaṃ te vipriyaṃ kānta kadā cid api saṃsmare sarvā vai vidhavā nārī bahuputrāpi khecara śocyā bhavati bandhūnāṃ patihīnā manasvinī
english: "I cannot recall, beloved, that I ever once did anything to displease you. Every widowed woman, O sky-ranger, even one with many sons, becomes an object of pity to her kin—a noble-hearted woman bereft of her husband."

sanskrit: lālitāhaṃ tvayā nityaṃ bahumānāc ca sāntvitā vacanair madhuraiḥ snigdhair asakṛt sumanoharaiḥ
english: "Ever was I cherished by you and soothed with great regard, again and again, with words sweet, tender, and most delightful."

sanskrit: kandareṣu ca śailānāṃ nadīnāṃ nirjhareṣu ca drumāgreṣu ca ramyeṣu ramitāhaṃ tvayā priya
english: "In the caverns of the mountains, by the cascades of the rivers, and on the lovely crowns of the trees, I was made happy by you, my beloved."

sanskrit: ākāśagamane caiva sukhitāhaṃ tvayā sukham vihṛtāsmi tvayā kānta tan me nādyāsti kiṃ cana
english: "In our flights through the sky I knew happiness with you, my love; I sported with you—but now none of that is left to me at all."

sanskrit: mitaṃ dadāti hi pitā mitaṃ mātā mitaṃ sutaḥ amitasya tu dātāraṃ bhartāraṃ kā na pūjayet
english: "A father gives but a measured portion, a mother a measured portion, a son a measured portion; but a husband, who gives without measure—what woman would not honor him?"

sanskrit: nāsti bhartṛsamo nātho na ca bhartṛsamaṃ sukham visṛjya dhanasarvasvaṃ bhartā vai śaraṇaṃ striyāḥ
english: "There is no protector like a husband, and no happiness like a husband; renouncing all her wealth and possessions, a woman's refuge is her husband alone."

sanskrit: na kāryam iha me nātha jīvitena tvayā vinā patihīnāpi kā nārī satī jīvitum utsahet
english: "I have no use, my lord, for life in this world without you. What virtuous woman bereft of her husband could bring herself to live?"

sanskrit: evaṃ vilapya bahudhā karuṇaṃ sā suduḥkhitā pativratā saṃpradīptaṃ praviveśa hutāśanam
english: Having lamented thus in many a piteous way, the deeply grieving, devoted wife entered the blazing fire.

sanskrit: tataś citrāmbaradharaṃ bhartāraṃ sānvapaśyata vimānasthaṃ sukṛtibhiḥ pūjyamānaṃ mahātmabhiḥ
english: Then she beheld her husband, clad in shining garments, seated in a celestial chariot, honored by the great-souled doers of good deeds.

sanskrit: citramālyāmbaradharaṃ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitam vimānaśatakoṭībhir āvṛtaṃ puṇyakīrtibhiḥ
english: He wore bright garlands and garments and was adorned with every ornament, surrounded by a hundred million celestial cars belonging to those of holy renown.

sanskrit: tataḥ svargagataḥ pakṣī bhāryayā saha saṃgataḥ karmaṇā pūjitas tena reme tatra sa bhāryayā
english: Then the bird, gone to heaven, was reunited with his wife; honored for that deed of his, he rejoiced there together with her.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca vimānasthau tu tau rājaṃl lubdhako vai dadarśa ha dṛṣṭvā tau daṃpatī duḥkhād acintayata sadgatim
english: Bhīṣma said: The fowler, O king, saw the pair seated in the celestial chariot; and seeing the husband and wife, he reflected, out of his grief, upon the good path.

sanskrit: kīdṛśeneha tapasā gaccheyaṃ paramāṃ gatim iti buddhyā viniścitya gamanāyopacakrame
english: "By what manner of austerity might I attain the supreme goal?" Having resolved this in his mind, he set out upon his journey.

sanskrit: mahāprasthānam āśritya lubdhakaḥ pakṣijīvanaḥ niśceṣṭo mārutāhāro nirmamaḥ svargakāṅkṣayā
english: Taking up the Great Departure, the fowler who had lived by killing birds became still, living on air alone, free of all sense of "mine," in longing for heaven.

sanskrit: tato 'paśyat suvistīrṇaṃ hṛdyaṃ padmavibhūṣitam nānādvijagaṇākīrṇaṃ saraḥ śītajalaṃ śubham pipāsārto 'pi tad dṛṣṭvā tṛptaḥ syān nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: Then he saw a broad and lovely lake, adorned with lotuses, thronged with flocks of many birds, its cool waters fair—a sight at which even one tormented by thirst would be satisfied, of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: upavāsakṛśo 'tyarthaṃ sa tu pārthiva lubdhakaḥ upasarpata saṃhṛṣṭaḥ śvāpadādhyuṣitaṃ vanam
english: But the fowler, O king, grown exceedingly gaunt with fasting, gladly approached a forest inhabited by beasts of prey.

sanskrit: mahāntaṃ niścayaṃ kṛtvā lubdhakaḥ praviveśa ha praviśann eva ca vanaṃ nigṛhītaḥ sa kaṇṭakaiḥ
english: Having made his great resolve, the fowler entered in; and even as he entered the forest, he was caught fast by thorns.

sanskrit: sa kaṇṭakavibhugnāṅgo lohitārdrīkṛtacchaviḥ babhrāma tasmin vijane nānāmṛgasamākule
english: His limbs torn by the thorns, his skin made wet with blood, he wandered through that desolate place teeming with all manner of wild beasts.

sanskrit: tato drumāṇāṃ mahatāṃ pavanena vane tadā udatiṣṭhata saṃgharṣāt sumahān havyavāhanaḥ
english: Then in that forest, from the friction of great trees driven by the wind, there arose a mighty fire, bearer of oblations.

sanskrit: tad vanaṃ vṛkṣasaṃkīrṇaṃ latāviṭapasaṃkulam dadāha pāvakaḥ kruddho yugāntāgnisamaprabhaḥ
english: That forest, dense with trees and tangled with creepers and boughs, the fire consumed in fury, blazing like the flame at the end of an age.

sanskrit: sajvālaiḥ pavanoddhūtair visphuliṅgaiḥ samanvitaḥ dadāha tad vanaṃ ghoraṃ mṛgapakṣisamākulam
english: Attended by flaming sparks fanned up by the wind, it burned that dreadful forest thronged with beasts and birds.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa dehamokṣārthaṃ saṃprahṛṣṭena cetasā abhyadhāvata saṃvṛddhaṃ pāvakaṃ lubdhakas tadā
english: Then, with a heart full of gladness, seeking the release of his body, the fowler ran toward that swelling fire.

sanskrit: tatas tenāgninā dagdho lubdhako naṣṭakilbiṣaḥ jagāma paramāṃ siddhiṃ tadā bharatasattama
english: Then, consumed by that fire, the fowler, his sins destroyed, attained the supreme perfection, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tataḥ svargastham ātmānaṃ so 'paśyad vigatajvaraḥ yakṣagandharvasiddhānāṃ madhye bhrājantam indravat
english: Then, his anguish gone, he beheld himself established in heaven, shining like Indra amid the yakṣas, gandharvas, and siddhas.

sanskrit: evaṃ khalu kapotaś ca kapotī ca pativratā lubdhakena saha svargaṃ gatāḥ puṇyena karmaṇā
english: Thus indeed the pigeon and the devoted hen-pigeon, together with the fowler, went to heaven through their meritorious deeds.

sanskrit: yāpi caivaṃvidhā nārī bhartāram anuvartate virājate hi sā kṣipraṃ kapotīva divi sthitā
english: And whatever woman of such a kind follows after her husband, she too shines forth at once, dwelling in heaven like that hen-pigeon.

sanskrit: evam etat purā vṛttaṃ lubdhakasya mahātmanaḥ kapotasya ca dharmiṣṭhā gatiḥ puṇyena karmaṇā
english: Thus did this come to pass of old: the righteous destiny, won through meritorious deeds, of the great-souled fowler and of the pigeon.

sanskrit: yaś cedaṃ śṛṇuyān nityaṃ yaś cedaṃ parikīrtayet nāśubhaṃ vidyate tasya manasāpi pramādyataḥ
english: Whoever should ever hear this, and whoever should recite it, no misfortune befalls him, even should his mind grow heedless.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira mahān eṣa dharmo dharmabhṛtāṃ vara goghneṣv api bhaved asmin niṣkṛtiḥ pāpakarmaṇaḥ niṣkṛtir na bhavet tasmin yo hanyāc charaṇāgatam
english: O Yudhiṣṭhira, great is this dharma, O best of the upholders of dharma. Even for slayers of cattle there may be expiation of their sinful deed; but there is no expiation for him who would slay one who has come to him for refuge.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca abuddhipūrvaṃ yaḥ pāpaṃ kuryād bharatasattama mucyate sa kathaṃ tasmād enasas tad vadasva me
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: One who commits a sin unknowingly, O best of the Bhāratas—how is he freed from that wrong? Tell me this.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atra te varṇayiṣye 'ham itihāsaṃ purātanam indrotaḥ śaunako vipro yad āha janamejayam
english: Bhīṣma said: On this matter I shall relate to you an ancient tale—what Indrota the brāhmaṇa, son of Śunaka, said to Janamejaya.

sanskrit: āsīd rājā mahāvīryaḥ pārikṣij janamejayaḥ abuddhipūrvaṃ brahmahatyā tam āgacchan mahīpatim
english: There was a king of great valor, Janamejaya, son of Parīkṣit; unwittingly, the slaying of a brāhmaṇa came upon that lord of the earth.

sanskrit: taṃ brāhmaṇāḥ sarva eva tatyajuḥ sapurohitāḥ jagāma sa vanaṃ rājā dahyamāno divāniśam
english: All the brāhmaṇas, together with his household priests, forsook him; and the king, burning day and night, went off to the forest.

sanskrit: sa prajābhiḥ parityaktaś cakāra kuśalaṃ mahat ativelaṃ tapas tepe dahyamānaḥ sa manyunā
english: Abandoned by his subjects, he did great works of merit; he practiced austerity beyond all measure, burning the while with remorse.

sanskrit: tatretihāsaṃ vakṣyāmi dharmasyāsyopabṛṃhaṇam dahyamānaḥ pāpakṛtyā jagāma janamejayaḥ
english: On this I shall tell a tale that confirms and amplifies this dharma: burning with his evil deed, Janamejaya set forth.

sanskrit: variṣyamāṇa indrotaṃ śaunakaṃ saṃśitavratam samāsādyopajagrāha pādayoḥ paripīḍayan
english: Wishing to choose him as priest, he came to Indrota, son of Śunaka, of firm-fixed vows, and clasped him, pressing hard upon his feet.

sanskrit: tato bhīto mahāprājño jagarhe subhṛśaṃ tadā kartā pāpasya mahato bhrūṇahā kim ihāgataḥ
english: Then the great sage, afraid, rebuked him most severely: "You who have wrought a great sin, slayer of an unborn child—why have you come here?"

sanskrit: kiṃ tavāsmāsu kartavyaṃ mā mā sprākṣīḥ kathaṃ cana gaccha gaccha na te sthānaṃ prīṇāty asmān iha dhruvam
english: "What is there for you to do with us? Touch me not, by any means whatever! Go, go—your presence here surely gives us no pleasure."
